items.title: Skeletal Ising fusion-data package
items.design_state: A-page local mathematical definition of exact Ising fusion channels, F-symbols and duality maps needed for the physical realization.
items.statement:
Let the scalar field be $\mathbb C$ and let the simple labels be $\mathbf 1$, $\psi$, and $\sigma$. Define a $\mathbb C$-linear semisimple category candidate whose objects are finite direct sums of these labels, whose simple-label Hom space is $\mathbb C$ when the labels agree and $0$ otherwise, and whose Hom spaces between direct sums are the corresponding finite matrices. Give the simple-label fusion product by

$$
\mathbf 1\otimes a=a\otimes\mathbf 1=a,\qquad \psi\otimes\psi=\mathbf 1,\qquad \psi\otimes\sigma=\sigma\otimes\psi=\sigma,\qquad \sigma\otimes\sigma=\mathbf 1\oplus\psi.
$$

Extend the product bilinearly to direct sums and on morphisms by the induced tensor product of scalar maps. The unit is $\mathbf 1$ and the unitors are strict. Fusion spaces are $V_{ab}^c=\operatorname{Hom}(a\otimes b,c)$; each is one-dimensional when the displayed fusion rule allows $c$ and is zero otherwise. In every allowed one-dimensional fusion space choose its displayed basis vector. On three simple labels, define the associator in these bases by the matrix $[F^{abc}_d]_{xy}$, where $x$ is the intermediate label in $(a\otimes b)\otimes c\to d$ and $y$ is the intermediate label in $a\otimes(b\otimes c)\to d$. Set

$$
\left[F^{\sigma\sigma\sigma}_{\sigma}\right]_{xy}=\frac{1}{\sqrt2}\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix}_{xy},\qquad x,y\in\{\mathbf 1,\psi\},
$$

$$
\left[F^{\psi\sigma\psi}_{\sigma}\right]_{\sigma\sigma}=-1,\qquad \left[F^{\sigma\psi\sigma}_{\psi}\right]_{\sigma\sigma}=-1.
$$

Every other coefficient is $1$ when all four fusion vertices are allowed and $0$ when any required fusion vertex is forbidden. Extend each associator linearly over direct sums. The candidate dual of each simple label is itself. For $\mathbf 1$ and $\psi$, take evaluation and coevaluation to be the unit-channel basis maps with coefficient $1$. For $\sigma$, take evaluation $\sigma\otimes\sigma\to\mathbf 1$ and coevaluation $\mathbf 1\to\sigma\otimes\sigma$ to have coefficient $2^{1/4}$ in the $\mathbf 1$ channel and zero in the $\psi$ channel. This item specifies the data; the separate coherence result checks that they satisfy the fusion-category axioms. No braiding or physical realization is included in this definition.

items.title: Coherence of the Ising fusion data
items.design_state: A-page local mathematical coherence result with an exact exhaustive pentagon check; no physical premises.
items.statement: For the complex-linear Ising fusion-data package with simple labels $\mathbf 1,\psi,\sigma$, fusion rules $\psi\otimes\psi\cong\mathbf 1$, $\psi\otimes\sigma\cong\sigma\otimes\psi\cong\sigma$, and $\sigma\otimes\sigma\cong\mathbf 1\oplus\psi$, with the associator and dual maps specified below, the associator satisfies the pentagon, the strict unitors satisfy the triangle, and the evaluation and coevaluation maps satisfy both snake identities. Consequently the package is a finite semisimple rigid monoidal category with simple unit, hence a finite semisimple fusion category. With the chosen fusion-space basis orthonormal and the standard Hermitian inner products, its associators are unitary.

items.title: Finite-lattice realization of the Ising non-invertible defect
items.design_state: Assigned conditional finite-lattice physical theorem with explicit Hamiltonian, defect operator, fusion and junction data.
items.statement:
Fix an integer $L\ge2$ and the periodic site set $\mathbb Z/L\mathbb Z$. Let $\mathcal H_L=\ell^2(\mathbb Z_2^L)$ with orthonormal basis $|h_1,\ldots,h_L\rangle$, where every $h_j\in\mathbb Z_2$ and $h_0=h_L$. Define Pauli operators by $Z_j|\mathbf h\rangle=(-1)^{h_j}|\mathbf h\rangle$ and $X_j|\mathbf h\rangle=|\mathbf h+\mathbf e_j\rangle$. Adopt the finite quantum Ising model with Hamiltonian

$$
H_L=-J\sum_{j=1}^{L}(Z_jZ_{j+1}+X_j),\qquad J>0,
$$

where $Z_{L+1}=Z_1$, $J$ has units of energy, and $\hbar=1$. Euclidean propagation through a time interval $s\ge0$ is the exact finite matrix $e^{-sH_L}$, with $s$ in inverse-energy units. Correlators are matrix elements between arbitrary boundary vectors of finite ordered lists of observable matrices and these propagation factors.

Let $\widehat{\mathcal H}_L=\ell^2(\mathbb Z_2^L)$ have basis $|\widehat h_{1/2},\ldots,\widehat h_{L-1/2}\rangle$, with dual Pauli operators $\widehat Z$ and $\widehat X$ defined by the same formulas on half-integer sites. Define the Kramers–Wannier defect map $D_L:\mathcal H_L\to\widehat{\mathcal H}_L$ by

$$
\langle\widehat{\mathbf h}|D_L|\mathbf h\rangle=2^{-L/2}(-1)^{\sum_{j=1}^{L}\widehat h_{j-1/2}(h_{j-1}+h_j)}.
$$

Identify the dual chain with the original chain by the half-site shift $j+1/2\mapsto j$; under this identification $D_L$ is an endodefect. A defect line is a wrapping insertion of $D_L$ on a Euclidean time slice. Its allowed position changes are slides within gaps between fixed observable insertions. In this finite lattice model, topologicality means invariance under the declared local line slides and re-association moves; no smooth continuum isotopy claim is made. A finite defect network has labels $\mathbf 1,\psi,\sigma$, represented on the chain by $I,P_L,D_L$, where $P_L=\prod_jX_j$. Its fusion spaces are one-dimensional precisely for

$$
\mathbf 1\otimes a=a\otimes\mathbf 1=a,\qquad \psi\otimes\psi=\mathbf 1,\qquad \psi\otimes\sigma=\sigma\otimes\psi=\sigma,\qquad \sigma\otimes\sigma=\mathbf 1\oplus\psi,
$$

and zero otherwise. Fix the Ising junction bases and associator as follows. Write $\epsilon(\mathbf 1)=0$ and $\epsilon(\psi)=1$; then

$$
[F^{\sigma\sigma\sigma}_{\sigma}]_{ab}=2^{-1/2}(-1)^{\epsilon(a)\epsilon(b)},\qquad a,b\in\{\mathbf 1,\psi\},
$$

$$
[F^{\psi\sigma\psi}_{\sigma}]_{\sigma\sigma}=-1,\qquad [F^{\sigma\psi\sigma}_{\psi}]_{\sigma\sigma}=-1,
$$

and every other allowed associator coefficient is $1$. In the local height basis, the nontrivial trivalent tensors with cyclic labels $(\sigma,\sigma,\psi)$ and $(\sigma,\psi,\sigma)$ are $2^{-1/4}(-1)^h$ and $(X)_{hh'}=\delta_{h',h+1}$, respectively; reversed orientations use adjoint tensors. Together with the unit-channel maps specified above, these are the adopted local junction and re-association data of this finite network model; they are not inferred from fusion multiplicities alone.

For this selected finite model, $D_L$ is topological under the declared defect slides, its exact operator fusion is $D_L^2=I+P_L$, $P_L^2=I$, and $D_LP_L=P_LD_L=D_L$, and the junction spaces and associators are the finite semisimple unitary Ising fusion data above. In particular $D_L$ is non-invertible. The claim is confined to this finite lattice model and asserts no continuum limit or empirical fact.
items.physical_scope: An exact finite periodic quantum Ising spin chain and its declared finite defect-network extension at the self-dual zero-field coupling; no infinite-volume, continuum-QFT, universality, or empirical claim is made.

title: Non-Invertible Symmetry Operators and Fusion — Examples

items.title: The Ising fusion object is simple and non-invertible
items.design_state: B-page abstract finite algebraic example using the exact local mathematical suppliers; no physical-realization claim.
items.statement: Let $\mathcal I$ be the complex finite semisimple fusion category with simple objects $\mathbf 1,\psi,\sigma$, fusion rules $\psi\otimes\psi\cong\mathbf 1$, $\psi\otimes\sigma\cong\sigma\otimes\psi\cong\sigma$, and $\sigma\otimes\sigma\cong\mathbf 1\oplus\psi$. Encode the intermediate labels by $\epsilon(\mathbf 1)=0$ and $\epsilon(\psi)=1$. Its coherent Ising associator has non-identity coefficients $[F^{\sigma\sigma\sigma}_{\sigma}]_{ab}=2^{-1/2}(-1)^{\epsilon(a)\epsilon(b)}$ for $a,b\in\{\mathbf 1,\psi\}$, $[F^{\psi\sigma\psi}_{\sigma}]_{\sigma\sigma}=-1$, and $[F^{\sigma\psi\sigma}_{\psi}]_{\sigma\sigma}=-1$; every other allowed associator coefficient is $1$. The simple object $\sigma$ has no right tensor inverse and is therefore a simple non-invertible object. This is an abstract algebraic example and makes no physical-realization claim.

references.title: Steven H. Simon, Topological Quantum, §§9.2–9.3
references.locator: PDF pp. 119–121 (book pagination approximately 103–105): Ising fusion rules, the simple duality object, and its fusion channels.

items.title: A non-invertible defect on a three-site Ising ring
items.design_state: B-page exact three-site finite-Hamiltonian example of a topological non-invertible defect; no continuum or empirical claim.
items.statement:
Let $\mathcal H_3=\ell^2(\mathbb Z_2^3)$ with orthonormal basis $|h_1,h_2,h_3\rangle$, and define $Z_j|\mathbf h\rangle=(-1)^{h_j}|\mathbf h\rangle$ and $X_j|\mathbf h\rangle=|\mathbf h+\mathbf e_j\rangle$. Use periodic indices and the finite Hamiltonian $H_3=-J\sum_{j=1}^3(Z_jZ_{j+1}+X_j)$, where $J>0$ has energy units and $\hbar=1$. Euclidean propagation through $s\ge0$ is $e^{-sH_3}$. Define $D_3$ from this ring to its half-shifted dual by

$$
\langle\widehat{\mathbf h}|D_3|\mathbf h\rangle=2^{-3/2}(-1)^{\sum_{j=1}^{3}\widehat h_{j-1/2}(h_{j-1}+h_j)},\qquad h_0=h_3,
$$

and identify dual sites with original sites by the half-shift. Let $P_3=X_1X_2X_3$ and $v=|000\rangle-|111\rangle$. The defect inserted on a Euclidean time slice is topological under the declared slides within gaps of fixed insertions, satisfies $D_3^2=I+P_3$, and annihilates $v$ after two fusions. Therefore this exact finite-model defect is non-invertible. No continuum or empirical claim is made.
items.physical_scope: An exact finite three-site periodic quantum Ising chain at the zero-field self-dual coupling, with an eight-dimensional Hilbert space; no infinite-volume, continuum, or empirical claim is made.
